args.summary: Release v2.3.1 of checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18% following the latest deploy. Mitigation: rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback, the service is healthy with an error rate of 0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was only validated in staging and was never healthy in production. Follow-up: investigate the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before attempting redeploy.
args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after latest deploy

trace.final:
Done. Summary of actions:

1. **Diagnosed**: checkout-api v2.3.1 was unhealthy in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. The most recent release that was healthy in production was **v2.3.0** (v2.3.1-rc was only validated in staging).
2. **Rolled back**: All production regions are now running v2.3.0. Verified the service is healthy again with a 0.2% error rate.
3. **Opened incident**: Created **INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. The incident describes the failure, the rollback to v2.3.0, current healthy status, and notes v2.3.1 was never healthy in production so redeploying it requires change-manager approval per policy.

But they're technically independent... I'll do rollback first, then incident referencing completed rollback.

transcript.content: Now I'll verify the rollback restored health, then open the incident.
